summary.plain: The E949 detector stopped kaons inside itself and watched what happened next, looking for the rare case of a kaon turning into a pion and invisible particles.
summary.technical: Stopped-kaon spectrometer at BNL, successor to the E787 apparatus, tracking the decay pion's range, energy and kinematics to isolate K+ -> pi+ nu nubar candidates from background.

technology.note: General description inferred from the stopped-kaon technique named in the sourced titles; a dedicated E949 detector-paper full text was not fetched this session.
technology.value: Stopped-kaon spectrometer: incoming kaons are brought to rest in an active target/scintillator stack, and the outgoing pion is tracked and its full decay chain (range, energy and kinematics) measured to reject backgrounds
